page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.3 GHz. It features 12 vCPUs derived from 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 48 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio, and operates on a KVM hypervisor. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data places this instance consistently in the average performance tier across most compute and memory workloads. It achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1574.38 and a multi-core score of 12320.1, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 6488.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 696.57 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 62.11 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The CPU supports AVX-512 vector extensions and VNNI, which aids in vector calculations, but lacks AMX support.

While the instance handles lighter LLM inference tasks adequately, processing 752.4 tokens per second on a 135M model, performance drops to a weak tier for larger models, yielding only 7.5 tokens per second on a 7B model. This indicates a clear tradeoff when attempting complex machine learning tasks without dedicated GPU hardware. The instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, Redis caching, and software compilation.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.3xlarge is an x86_64 server instance featuring a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.3 GHz with 12 vCPUs and 48 GB of RAM. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Benchmark results place the instance in the average tier for general compute and memory tasks, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6488.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 13512.48. It demonstrates solid performance for static web serving at 9.92 GB/sec and Redis operations at 11.15 million operations per second. However, a significant performance tradeoff is evident in machine learning workloads, where text generation speeds drop to a weak 7.5 tokens per second for 7B models. It is best suited for general-purpose application hosting, software compilation, and caching.
